entry.title: Research Summary: April 07, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by a striking convergence of findings on human-AI interaction risks and AI safety mechanisms, alongside notable advances in biomedical AI and mathematical reasoning.

  • Two large-scale RCTs (N=1,222 and N=2,012) deliver causal evidence that AI assistance reduces human persistence and that LLM-driven commercial persuasion nearly triples sponsored product selection rates (61.2% vs 22.4%). A complementary study identifies a Persuasion Paradox where LLM explanations increase user confidence without improving accuracy.
  • Mechanistic interpretability advances with the discovery of sparse gate-amplifier routing circuits underlying alignment in LLMs, validated across multiple model families. A cryptographic result from Vaikuntanathan shows AI agents can conduct undetectable secret conversations via pseudorandom noise-resilient key exchange—a fundamental safety concern.
  • The first real-world safety audit of OpenClaw, a deployed personal AI agent, introduces the CIK taxonomy for evaluating agent risks at scale. A 10,000-trial taxonomy systematically maps which prompt features trigger LLM agents to exploit vulnerabilities.
  • In biomedical AI, STORM bridges spatial transcriptomics and histology across 1.2M profiles and 18 organs. QED-Nano demonstrates a 4B-parameter model achieving competitive theorem proving. Nobel laureate Acemoglu models how AI aggregation can destabilize social learning beyond a critical update-speed threshold.

entry.title: AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance

author.name: Grace Liu, Brian Christian, Tsvetomira Dumbalska, Michiel A. Bakker, Rachit Dubey

entry.summary: Through randomized controlled trials (N=1,222), provides causal evidence that AI assistance reduces human persistence and impairs unassisted performance across mathematical reasoning and reading tasks, showing current AI systems are 'short-sighted collaborators.'

entry.title: Commercial Persuasion in AI-Mediated Conversations

author.name: Francesco Salvi, Alejandro Cuevas, Manoel Horta Ribeiro

entry.summary: Two preregistered experiments (N=2,012) show LLM-driven commercial persuasion nearly triples sponsored product selection rates (61.2% vs 22.4% for search), while users remain largely unaware of the influence.

entry.title: A Multimodal Foundation Model of Spatial Transcriptomics and Histology for Biological Discovery and Clinical Prediction

author.name: Jinxi Xiang, Siyu Hou, Yuchen Li, Ryan Quinton, Xiaoming Zhang, Feyisope Eweje, Xiangde Luo, Yijiang Chen, Zhe Li, Colin Bergstrom, Ted Kim, Sierra Willens, Francesca Maria Olguin, Matthew Abikenari, Andrew Heider, Sanjeeth Rajaram, Joel Neal, Maximilian Diehn, Xiang Zhou, Ruijiang Li

entry.summary: Presents STORM, a foundation model trained on 1.2M spatially resolved transcriptomic profiles with matched histology across 18 organs, bridging imaging and omics through hierarchical morphological-molecular representations.

entry.title: QED-Nano: Teaching a Tiny Model to Prove Hard Theorems

author.name: LM-Provers, Yuxiao Qu, Amrith Setlur, Jasper Dekoninck, Edward Beeching, Jia Li, Ian Wu, Lewis Tunstall, Aviral Kumar

entry.summary: QED-Nano is a 4B parameter model post-trained for Olympiad-level mathematical proofs using a three-stage recipe: supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and curriculum learning. It demonstrates that small, open models can achieve competitive reasoning on hard mathematical problems.

entry.title: How Alignment Routes: Localizing, Scaling, and Controlling Policy Circuits in Language Models

author.name: Gregory N. Frank

entry.summary: Identifies a sparse routing mechanism in alignment-trained LLMs where gate attention heads detect content and trigger amplifier heads for refusal, validated across 9 models from 6 labs with rigorous statistical tests.

entry.title: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw

author.name: Zijun Wang, Haoqin Tu, Letian Zhang, Hardy Chen, Juncheng Wu, Xiangyan Liu, Zhenlong Yuan, Tianyu Pang, Michael Qizhe Shieh, Fengze Liu, Zeyu Zheng, Huaxiu Yao, Yuyin Zhou, Cihang Xie

entry.summary: Presents the first real-world safety evaluation of OpenClaw, a widely deployed personal AI agent in early 2026, introducing the CIK taxonomy (Capability, Identity, Knowledge) and testing 12 attack scenarios across four backbone models including Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.

entry.title: Olmo Hybrid: From Theory to Practice and Back

author.name: William Merrill, Yanhong Li, Tyler Romero, Anej Svete, Caia Costello, Pradeep Dasigi, Dirk Groeneveld, David Heineman, Bailey Kuehl, Nathan Lambert, Jacob Morrison, Luca Soldaini, Finbarr Timbers, Pete Walsh, Noah A. Smith, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Ashish Sabharwal

entry.summary: Introduces OLMo Hybrid, a 7B-parameter model mixing recurrence and attention, with theoretical and empirical evidence that hybrid models surpass both pure transformers and linear RNNs in expressivity, including code execution tasks.

entry.title: When Do Hallucinations Arise? A Graph Perspective on the Evolution of Path Reuse and Path Compression

author.name: Xinnan Dai, Kai Yang, Cheng Luo, Shenglai Zeng, Kai Guo, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Models LLM next-token prediction as graph search, identifying two mechanisms causing hallucinations: path reuse (shortcutting through familiar routes) and path compression (collapsing multi-hop reasoning). Provides a structural theory of when hallucinations arise.

entry.title: ShieldNet: Network-Level Guardrails against Emerging Supply-Chain Injections in Agentic Systems

author.name: Zhuowen Yuan, Zhaorun Chen, Zhen Xiang, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Seyyed Hadi Hashemi, Chaowei Xiao, Wenbo Guo, Bo Li

entry.summary: Introduces SC-Inject-Bench, a benchmark of 10,000+ malicious MCP tools covering 25+ attack types, and proposes ShieldNet for network-level defense against supply-chain attacks in agentic systems.

entry.title: The Persuasion Paradox: When LLM Explanations Fail to Improve Human-AI Team Performance

author.name: Ruth Cohen, Lu Feng, Ayala Bloch, Sarit Kraus

entry.summary: Identifies a 'Persuasion Paradox' where LLM explanations systematically increase user confidence and reliance on AI without reliably improving task accuracy, demonstrated across visual reasoning (RAVEN matrices) and logical reasoning (LSAT) tasks in three controlled studies.

entry.title: An Improved Last-Iterate Convergence Rate for Anchored Gradient Descent Ascent

author.name: Anja Surina, Arun Suggala, George Tsoukalas, Anton Kovsharov, Sergey Shirobokov, Francisco J. R. Ruiz, Pushmeet Kohli, Swarat Chaudhuri

entry.summary: Proves improved O(1/t) last-iterate convergence rate for Anchored Gradient Descent Ascent for convex-concave min-max problems, resolving an open question. Notably, the result was discovered by an AI system writing formal Lean proofs.

entry.title: Mapping the Exploitation Surface: A 10,000-Trial Taxonomy of What Makes LLM Agents Exploit Vulnerabilities

author.name: Charafeddine Mouzouni

entry.summary: Systematic taxonomy from ~10,000 trials mapping which prompt features trigger LLM agents to exploit security vulnerabilities, finding that only 3 of 12 hypothesized dimensions (authority framing, goal anchoring, euphemistic relabeling) are effective triggers.

entry.title: Undetectable Conversations Between AI Agents via Pseudorandom Noise-Resilient Key Exchange

author.name: Vinod Vaikuntanathan, Or Zamir

entry.summary: Shows that two AI agents can conduct secret parallel conversations producing transcripts computationally indistinguishable from honest interactions, even against strong passive auditors. Establishes that without a shared secret key, such covert communication is impossible under standard assumptions.

entry.title: Vero: An Open RL Recipe for General Visual Reasoning

author.name: Gabriel Sarch, Linrong Cai, Qunzhong Wang, Haoyang Wu, Danqi Chen, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Vero, a family of fully open VLMs trained with RL across six task categories using 600K samples from 59 datasets. Achieves SOTA among open-weight models across diverse visual reasoning tasks with a transparent recipe.

entry.title: AIs can now often do massive easy-to-verify SWE tasks and I've updated towards shorter timelines

author.name: ryan_greenblatt

entry.summary: Ryan Greenblatt (Redwood Research) reports updating to ~30% probability of full AI R&D automation by EOY 2028 (up from ~15%). Expects AIs to achieve 50% reliability on massive easy-to-verify SWE tasks with years-to-decades time horizons by EOY 2026.

entry.title: Don't Blink: Evidence Collapse during Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Suresh Raghu, Satwik Pandey

entry.summary: Discovers 'evidence collapse' in reasoning VLMs: attention to visual evidence regions drops substantially as reasoning progresses, creating confident but visually ungrounded predictions that text-only monitoring cannot detect.

entry.title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Histopathology

author.name: Jinxi Xiang, Mingjie Li, Siyu Hou, Yijiang Chen, Xiangde Luo, Yuanfeng Ji, Xiang Zhou, Ehsan Adeli, Akshay Chaudhari, Curtis P. Langlotz, Kilian M. Pohl, Ruijiang Li

entry.summary: MuPD is a generative foundation model for multimodal histopathology that embeds H&E histology, molecular RNA profiles, and clinical text into a shared latent space via diffusion transformer. Pretrained on 100 million+ data points for cross-modal generation and imputation.

entry.title: Justified or Just Convincing? Error Verifiability as a Dimension of LLM Quality

author.name: Xiaoyuan Zhu, Kimberly Le Truong, Riccardo Fogliato, Gokul Swamy, Weijian Zhang, Minglai Yang, Longtian Ye, Bangya Liu, Minghao Liu, Andrew Ilyas, Steven Wu

entry.summary: Formalizes 'error verifiability' - whether LLM justifications help users distinguish correct from incorrect answers - and proposes a balanced metric. Finds that common approaches like post-training and scaling don't improve verifiability.

entry.title: How AI Aggregation Affects Knowledge

author.name: Daron Acemoglu, Tianyi Lin, Asuman Ozdaglar, James Siderius

entry.summary: Studies how AI aggregation affects social learning using an extended DeGroot model. Shows a threshold effect: when an AI aggregator updates too quickly, it cannot robustly improve learning, but slow updating allows improvement.

entry.title: Self-Execution Simulation Improves Coding Models

author.name: Gallil Maimon, Ori Yoran, Felix Kreuk, Michael Hassid, Gal Cohen, Pierre Chambon, Yossi Adi

entry.summary: Demonstrates that Code LLMs can be trained to simulate program execution step-by-step using natural language execution traces and RL with verifiable rewards, improving competitive programming performance. Introduces output prediction and self-predicted execution objectives.

entry.title: Position: Science of AI Evaluation Requires Item-level Benchmark Data

author.name: Han Jiang, Susu Zhang, Xiaoyuan Yi, Xing Xie, Ziang Xiao

entry.summary: Argues that item-level benchmark data (individual question responses, not just aggregate scores) is essential for building a rigorous science of AI evaluation. Identifies systemic validity failures in current evaluation paradigms and proposes granular diagnostic analysis.

entry.title: Implementing surrogate goals for safer bargaining in LLM-based agents

author.name: Caspar Oesterheld, Maxime Rich\'e, Filip Sondej, Jesse Clifton, Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: Implements surrogate goals in LLM-based agents to reduce bargaining failure risks. Tests whether agents can be made to care about proxy costs (e.g., money burning) to deflect threats from principal's actual interests.

entry.title: Why Attend to Everything? Focus is the Key

author.name: Hengshuai Yao, Xing Chen, Ahmed Murtadha, Jin Li, Shuai Shao, Yasin Abbasi Yadkori, Guan Wang, Mingli Yuan, William Chen, Sen Song

entry.summary: Introduces Focus, a method that learns which token pairs matter via learnable centroids, restricting distant attention to same-group pairs while maintaining local full-resolution attention. It's purely additive with frozen weights and improves perplexity from 124M to 70B scale.

entry.title: The Augmentation Trap: AI Productivity and the Cost of Cognitive Offloading

author.name: Michael Caosun, Sinan Aral

entry.summary: Develops a dynamic model analyzing the 'augmentation trap' where AI tools boost immediate productivity but erode worker expertise over time. Shows that rational adoption can lead to steady-state productivity loss, and that managerial myopia amplifies these costs.

entry.title: Three Phases of Expert Routing: How Load Balance Evolves During Mixture-of-Experts Training

author.name: Charafeddine Mouzouni

entry.summary: Models MoE token routing as a congestion game and identifies three distinct phases during training: surge, stabilization, and relaxation. Validates across OLMoE and OpenMoE checkpoints.

entry.title: Grokking as Dimensional Phase Transition in Neural Networks

author.name: Ping Wang

entry.summary: Characterizes neural network grokking as a dimensional phase transition where effective dimensionality crosses from sub-diffusive to super-diffusive at generalization onset, exhibiting self-organized criticality.

entry.title: Cog-DRIFT: Exploration on Adaptively Reformulated Instances Enables Learning from Hard Reasoning Problems

author.name: Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Archiki Prasad, Zaid Khan, Joykirat Singh, Runchu Tian, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: Proposes Cog-DRIFT, which transforms hard open-ended reasoning problems into cognitively simpler variants (multiple-choice, cloze) to enable learning from problems too difficult for RLVR. Models bootstrap from easier formats to harder ones, achieving gains on math and science benchmarks.

entry.title: From Curiosity to Caution: Mitigating Reward Hacking for Best-of-N with Pessimism

author.name: Zhuohao Yu, Zhiwei Steven Wu, Adam Block

entry.summary: Addresses reward hacking in Best-of-N sampling for LLMs by proposing a pessimistic approach to reward model scoring. Shows that existing approaches (stronger reward models, distributional regularization) fail to reliably mitigate hacking as N increases.

entry.title: MinerU2.5-Pro: Pushing the Limits of Data-Centric Document Parsing at Scale

author.name: Bin Wang, Tianyao He, Linke Ouyang, Fan Wu, Zhiyuan Zhao, Tao Chu, Yuan Qu, Zhenjiang Jin, Weijun Zeng, Ziyang Miao, Bangrui Xu, Junbo Niu, Mengzhang Cai, Jiantao Qiu, Qintong Zhang, Dongsheng Ma, Yuefeng Sun, Hejun Dong, Wenzheng Zhang, Jutao Xiao, Jiayong Shi, Pengyu Liao, Xiaomeng Zhao, Huaping Zhong, Liqun Wei, Jing Yu, Jie Yang, Wei Li, Shasha Wang, Qianqian Wu, Xuanhe Zhou, Weijia Li, Zhenxiang Li, Zhongying Tu, Jiang Wu, Lijun Wu, Chao Xu, Kai Chen, Wentao Zhang, Yu Qiao, Bowen Zhou, Dahua Lin, Conghui He

entry.summary: Presents MinerU2.5-Pro, advancing document parsing SOTA purely through data engineering while keeping a fixed 1.2B-parameter architecture. Demonstrates that performance bottlenecks stem from training data deficiencies rather than architecture, as SOTA models show consistent failure patterns on hard samples. Built around a Data Engine focused on coverage, informativeness, and annotation accuracy.

entry.title: A Frame is Worth One Token: Efficient Generative World Modeling with Delta Tokens

author.name: Tommie Kerssies, Gabriele Berton, Ju He, Qihang Yu, Wufei Ma, Daan de Geus, Gijs Dubbelman, Liang-Chieh Chen

entry.summary: DeltaTok encodes VFM feature differences between consecutive video frames into single continuous 'delta' tokens, enabling DeltaWorld, a generative world model that efficiently predicts future states with one token per frame.

entry.title: Veo-Act: How Far Can Frontier Video Models Advance Generalizable Robot Manipulation?

author.name: Zhongru Zhang, Chenghan Yang, Qingzhou Lu, Yanjiang Guo, Jianke Zhang, Yucheng Hu, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: Investigates using Google's Veo-3 video generation model for zero-shot robotic manipulation: Veo-3 predicts future image sequences from observations, and an inverse dynamics model (trained only on random-play data) recovers robot actions. No human demonstrations needed.

entry.title: Selective Forgetting for Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Tuan Le, Wei Qian, Mengdi Huai

entry.summary: Addresses machine unlearning for Large Reasoning Models that generate chains of thought, proposing methods to selectively forget sensitive information from reasoning traces without degrading general reasoning ability.

entry.title: Readable Minds: Emergent Theory-of-Mind-Like Behavior in LLM Poker Agents

author.name: Hsieh-Ting Lin, Tsung-Yu Hou

entry.summary: Reports that LLM agents playing Texas Hold'em poker progressively develop theory-of-mind-like opponent modeling, but only when equipped with persistent memory. Memory is both necessary and sufficient; domain knowledge is neither.

entry.title: The Ideation Bottleneck: Decomposing the Quality Gap Between AI-Generated and Human Economics Research

author.name: Ning Li

entry.summary: Decomposes the quality gap between AI-generated and human economics research papers into idea quality vs execution quality, finding that the bottleneck is primarily in ideation. Analyzes 953 papers including 912 AI-generated from the APE project.

entry.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI

author.name: Nathanael Jo, Manish Raghavan

entry.summary: Through a pre-registered RCT, shows that incentives mediate AI's homogenizing effect in creative writing. Participants rewarded for originality produce more diverse writing even when using AI, driven by how they use AI rather than whether they use it.

entry.title: Geometric Limits of Knowledge Distillation: A Minimum-Width Theorem via Superposition Theory

author.name: Dawar Jyoti Deka, Nilesh Sarkar

entry.summary: Proposes a geometric theory for knowledge distillation limits based on superposition theory: student capacity is bounded by width × sparsity function, creating an irreducible loss floor when teacher features exceed this budget.

entry.title: Poisoned Identifiers Survive LLM Deobfuscation: A Case Study on Claude Opus 4.6

author.name: Luis Guzm\'an Lorenzo

entry.summary: Demonstrates that poisoned identifier names in JavaScript persist through Claude Opus 4.6's deobfuscation even when the model correctly understands the code semantics, revealing a dissociation between understanding and output.

entry.title: Darkness Visible: Reading the Exception Handler of a Language Model

author.name: Peter Balogh

entry.summary: Discovers that GPT-2 Small's final MLP layer contains a fully legible 27-neuron routing program organized as a three-tier exception handler, while showing the knowledge it routes remains entangled across ~3,040 residual neurons. Identifies a sharp consensus-exception crossover.

entry.title: The Format Tax

author.name: Ivan Yee Lee, Loris D'Antoni, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick

entry.summary: Shows that structured output format requirements (JSON, XML, LaTeX, Markdown) substantially degrade LLM reasoning and writing performance, with the dominant cost coming from format-requesting instructions in the prompt rather than constrained decoding.

entry.title: OP-GRPO: Efficient Off-Policy GRPO for Flow-Matching Models

author.name: Liyu Zhang, Kehan Li, Tingrui Han, Tao Zhao, Yuxuan Sheng, Shibo He, Chao Li

entry.summary: OP-GRPO introduces the first off-policy GRPO framework for flow-matching models, using replay buffers with high-quality trajectory selection, sequence-level importance sampling, and theoretical convergence guarantees. Achieves up to 2x sample efficiency improvement.

entry.title: Causality Laundering: Denial-Feedback Leakage in Tool-Calling LLM Agents

author.name: Mohammad Hossein Chinaei

entry.summary: Identifies 'causality laundering' in tool-calling LLM agents where adversaries exploit denial feedback to leak information through subsequent benign tool calls. Proposes Agentic Reference Monitor (ARM) for runtime enforcement.

entry.title: Early Stopping for Large Reasoning Models via Confidence Dynamics

author.name: Parsa Hosseini, Sumit Nawathe, Mahdi Salmani, Meisam Razaviyayn, Soheil Feizi

entry.summary: Proposes CoDE-Stop, an early stopping method for large reasoning models that monitors confidence dynamics of intermediate answers during chain-of-thought generation, reducing computation by stopping when high-confidence answers are reached.

entry.title: Think in Strokes, Not Pixels: Process-Driven Image Generation via Interleaved Reasoning

author.name: Lei Zhang, Junjiao Tian, Zhipeng Fan, Kunpeng Li, Jialiang Wang, Weifeng Chen, Markos Georgopoulos, Felix Juefei-Xu, Yuxiang Bao, Julian McAuley, Manling Li, Zecheng He

entry.summary: Introduces process-driven image generation that decomposes synthesis into interleaved reasoning trajectories of planning, drafting, reflection, and refinement, mimicking how humans paint incrementally with intermediate visual states.

entry.title: PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training

author.name: Erhan Zhang, Yiqun Chen, Zechun Niu, Wei Yang, Xiaochi Wei, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao

entry.summary: Introduces PRAISE, a framework that reuses prefix states from complete search trajectories and generates intermediate step rewards to improve data efficiency and credit assignment in agentic search RL training.

entry.title: LightThinker++: From Reasoning Compression to Memory Management

author.name: Yuqi Zhu, Jintian Zhang, Zhenjie Wan, Yujie Luo, Shuofei Qiao, Zhengke Gui, Da Zheng, Lei Liang, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: LightThinker++ enables LLMs to dynamically compress intermediate reasoning thoughts into compact representations, with explicit adaptive memory management primitives (store, retrieve, forget) for handling complex reasoning chains.

entry.title: ClawArena: Benchmarking AI Agents in Evolving Information Environments

author.name: Haonian Ji, Kaiwen Xiong, Siwei Han, Peng Xia, Shi Qiu, Yiyang Zhou, Jiaqi Liu, Jinlong Li, Bingzhou Li, Zeyu Zheng, Cihang Xie, Huaxiu Yao

entry.summary: Introduces ClawArena, a benchmark for AI agents operating in evolving information environments with contradictory sources, temporal updates, and implicit user corrections.

entry.title: Muon Dynamics as a Spectral Wasserstein Flow

author.name: Gabriel Peyr\'e

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of Muon optimizer dynamics through spectral Wasserstein distances, introducing a family of spectral normalization rules and studying them in a mean-field regime. Unifies gradient descent, Muon, and Schatten-type schemes.

entry.title: Are Latent Reasoning Models Easily Interpretable?

author.name: Connor Dilgren, Sarah Wiegreffe

entry.summary: Investigates interpretability of latent reasoning models (LRMs), finding that latent reasoning tokens are often unnecessary for predictions on logical reasoning tasks. LRMs can produce the same answers without latent reasoning, questioning their utility.

entry.title: Saliency-R1: Enforcing Interpretable and Faithful Vision-language Reasoning via Saliency-map Alignment Reward

author.name: Shizhan Gong, Minda Hu, Qiyuan Zhang, Chen Ma, Qi Dou

entry.summary: Saliency-R1 improves VLM interpretability and faithfulness by introducing a saliency map technique that highlights critical image regions for generated tokens, used as a reward signal in reinforcement learning to align visual reasoning with visual evidence.

entry.title: BioAlchemy: Distilling Biological Literature into Reasoning-Ready Reinforcement Learning Training Data

author.name: Brian Hsu, Ozan G\"okdemir, Carlo Siebenschuh, Bruce Parrello, Neil Getty, Thomas S. Brettin, Rick L. Stevens, Ian T. Foster, Nicholas Chia, Arvind Ramanathan

entry.summary: Introduces BioAlchemy, a pipeline for extracting verifiable question-answer pairs from biological literature to create reasoning-ready RL training data. Shows current biology questions in reasoning datasets don't match modern research topic distributions.

entry.title: InferenceEvolve: Towards Automated Causal Effect Estimators through Self-Evolving AI

author.name: Can Wang, Hongyu Zhao, Yiqun Chen

entry.summary: Introduces InferenceEvolve, an evolutionary framework using LLMs to discover and iteratively refine causal inference methods. Best evolved estimator reached the Pareto frontier against 58 human submissions in a competition.

entry.title: PanLUNA: An Efficient and Robust Query-Unified Multimodal Model for Edge Biosignal Intelligence

author.name: Marija Zelic, Anna Tegon, Yawei Li, Thorir Mar Ingolfsson, Luca Benini

entry.summary: Presents PanLUNA, a compact 5.4M-parameter pan-modal foundation model that jointly processes EEG, ECG, and PPG in a single encoder, matching or exceeding models 57x larger while being robust to missing modalities.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Quantization via Weight-Space Arithmetic

author.name: Daniele Solombrino, Antonio Andrea Gargiulo, Adrian Robert Minut, Luca Zhou, Alessandro Zirilli, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: Shows that robustness to post-training quantization is a transferable direction in weight space (a 'quantization vector') that can be extracted from a donor task and applied to a receiver model, improving PTQ robustness by up to 60% without QAT.

entry.title: MetaSAEs: Joint Training with a Decomposability Penalty Produces More Atomic Sparse Autoencoder Latents

author.name: Matthew Levinson

entry.summary: Introduces MetaSAEs, a joint training objective for sparse autoencoders that penalizes subspace blending using a small meta-SAE, producing more atomic latents that represent single coherent concepts for safer interpretability applications.

entry.title: Vocabulary Dropout for Curriculum Diversity in LLM Co-Evolution

author.name: Jacob Dineen, Aswin RRV, Zhikun Xu, Ben Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces vocabulary dropout—a random mask on proposer output logits—to prevent diversity collapse in co-evolutionary self-play for LLM training. Shows improvements on mathematical reasoning benchmarks using Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B models.

entry.title: SecPI: Secure Code Generation with Reasoning Models via Security Reasoning Internalization

author.name: Hao Wang, Niels M\"undler, Mark Vero, Jingxuan He, Dawn Song, Martin Vechev

entry.summary: SecPI is a fine-tuning pipeline that teaches reasoning language models to internalize structured security reasoning for code generation, producing secure code by default without inference-time prompts. Addresses the critical gap of security vulnerabilities in RLM-generated code.

entry.title: Can LLMs Learn to Reason Robustly under Noisy Supervision?

author.name: Shenzhi Yang, Guangcheng Zhu, Bowen Song, Sharon Li, Haobo Wang, Xing Zheng, Yingfan Ma, Zhongqi Chen, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: First systematic study of noisy label effects in RLVR, distinguishing between inactive noise (reduces efficiency) and active noise (causes harm). Shows that rollout-based conditioning naturally filters some noise.

entry.title: Many Preferences, Few Policies: Towards Scalable Language Model Personalization

author.name: Cheol Woo Kum, Jai Moondra, Roozbeh Nahavandi, Andrew Perrault, Milind Tambe, Swati Gupta

entry.summary: Addresses LLM personalization by developing PALM, an algorithm that selects a small portfolio of aligned LLMs to cover diverse user preferences across multiple traits, avoiding the need for per-user models.

entry.title: Compressible Softmax-Attended Language under Incompressible Attention

author.name: Wonsuk Lee

entry.summary: Empirically demonstrates across five transformer models (124M-7B) that the logit energy field in attention reaches 90% variance in 2-11 singular components, while the learned interaction matrix needs 38-75 components, revealing a 5-25x spectral gap.

entry.title: GAIN: Multiplicative Modulation for Domain Adaptation

author.name: Hengshuai Yao, Xing Chen, Ahmed Murtadha, Guan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes GAIN, a multiplicative modulation method inspired by neuroscience gain modulation that adapts LLMs to new domains while preserving old domain performance, unlike LoRA which causes forgetting.

entry.title: Hallucination Basins: A Dynamic Framework for Understanding and Controlling LLM Hallucinations

author.name: Kalyan Cherukuri, Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: Presents a geometric dynamical systems framework for understanding LLM hallucinations as task-dependent basin structures in latent space. Shows that basin separability is strongly task-dependent and that geometry-aware steering can reduce hallucination rates.

entry.title: Entropy, Disagreement, and the Limits of Foundation Models in Genomics

author.name: Maxime Rochkoulets, Lovro Vr\v{c}ek, Mile \v{S}iki\'c

entry.summary: Investigates why genomic foundation models underperform compared to NLP counterparts, attributing this to the high entropy of DNA sequences that leads to near-uniform output distributions and unstable embeddings. This is a valuable diagnostic study that explains a fundamental limitation in an important application domain.

entry.title: Isokinetic Flow Matching for Pathwise Straightening of Generative Flows

author.name: Tauhid Khan

entry.summary: Introduces Isokinetic Flow Matching (Iso-FM), a lightweight regularizer that penalizes pathwise acceleration in flow matching using self-guided finite-difference approximation, dramatically improving few-step sampling without requiring auxiliary encoders or second-order autodiff.

entry.title: Predict, Don't React: Value-Based Safety Forecasting for LLM Streaming

author.name: Pride Kavumba, Koki Wataoka, Huy H. Nguyen, Jiaxuan Li, Masaya Ohagi

entry.summary: Introduces StreamGuard, a model-agnostic streaming guardrail for LLMs that formulates moderation as a forecasting problem over partial prefixes using Monte Carlo rollout supervision, rather than boundary detection.

entry.title: Knowledge Packs: Zero-Token Knowledge Delivery via KV Cache Injection

author.name: Andrey Pustovit

entry.summary: Proposes Knowledge Packs: pre-computed KV caches that deliver knowledge at zero token cost for RAG, exploiting the causal mask property that KV cache from text F is identical to a joint pass on F+query. Achieves up to 95% token savings with zero divergence when correctly formatted.

entry.title: Full-Duplex-Bench-v3: Benchmarking Tool Use for Full-Duplex Voice Agents Under Real-World Disfluency

author.name: Guan-Ting Lin, Chen Chen, Zhehuai Chen, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Introduces Full-Duplex-Bench-v3, benchmarking spoken language models under real human speech disfluencies with multi-step tool use. Evaluates GPT-Realtime, Gemini Live 2.5/3.1, Grok, Ultravox v0.7, and cascaded pipelines across accuracy, latency, and turn-taking. First benchmark combining naturalistic speech conditions with chained API calls.

entry.title: 4C4D: 4 Camera 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Junsheng Zhou, Zhifan Yang, Liang Han, Wenyuan Zhang, Kanle Shi, Shenkun Xu, Yu-Shen Liu

entry.summary: 4C4D enables high-fidelity 4D dynamic scene reconstruction from only four portable cameras, dramatically reducing the dozens-to-hundreds of cameras typically required. Key innovation is a Neural Decaying Function on Gaussian opacities to handle the harder geometry learning under sparse settings.

entry.title: The Indra Representation Hypothesis for Multimodal Alignment

author.name: Jianglin Lu, Hailing Wang, Kuo Yang, Yitian Zhang, Simon Jenni, Yun Fu

entry.summary: Proposes The Indra Representation Hypothesis, arguing that unimodal foundation models converge to shared relational structures, formalized using category theory (V-enriched Yoneda embedding). Used to develop a multimodal alignment approach.

entry.title: Fully Procedural Synthetic Data from Simple Rules for Multi-View Stereo

author.name: Zeyu Ma, Alexander Raistrick, Jia Deng

entry.summary: Demonstrates that fully procedural synthetic data generated from simple NURBS rules can match or exceed manually curated training data for multi-view stereo, achieving strong results with just a small set of geometric primitives.

entry.title: FactReview: Evidence-Grounded Reviews with Literature Positioning and Execution-Based Claim Verification

author.name: Hang Xu, Ling Yue, Chaoqian Ouyang, Libin Zheng, Shaowu Pan, Shimin Di, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: Presents FactReview, an LLM-based paper reviewing system that combines claim extraction, literature retrieval, and execution-based verification (running released code) for evidence-grounded reviews.

entry.title: Combee: Scaling Prompt Learning for Self-Improving Language Model Agents

author.name: Hanchen Li, Runyuan He, Qizheng Zhang, Changxiu Ji, Qiuyang Mang, Xiaokun Chen, Lakshya A Agrawal, Wei-Liang Liao, Eric Yang, Alvin Cheung, James Zou, Kunle Olukotun, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez

entry.summary: Introduces Combee, a framework for scaling prompt learning in parallel for self-improving LLM agents, addressing quality degradation with high parallelism through principled scaling strategies.

entry.title: Decocted Experience Improves Test-Time Inference in LLM Agents

author.name: Maohao Shen, Kaiwen Zha, Zexue He, Zhang-Wei Hong, Siru Ouyang, J. Jon Ryu, Prasanna Sattigeri, Suhas Diggavi, Gregory Wornell

entry.summary: Shows that 'decocted experience'—carefully constructed context from prior agent runs—is a complementary scaling axis to test-time compute for improving LLM agent performance without parameter updates.

entry.title: MolDA: Molecular Understanding and Generation via Large Language Diffusion Model

author.name: Seohyeon Shin, HanJun Choi, Jun-Hyung Park, Hongkook Kim, Mansu Kim

entry.summary: Proposes MolDA, a multimodal molecular framework replacing autoregressive backbones with discrete Large Language Diffusion Models for molecular generation, addressing limitations of left-to-right generation for chemical validity.

entry.title: Robust LLM Performance Certification via Constrained Maximum Likelihood Estimation

author.name: Minghe Shen, Ananth Balashankar, Adam Fisch, David Madras, Miguel Rodrigues

entry.summary: Proposes a constrained maximum-likelihood estimation approach for LLM failure rate estimation that integrates human labels, LLM-as-judge annotations, and domain-specific constraints to achieve reliable failure rate estimates at lower cost.

entry.title: Large Language Models Align with the Human Brain during Creative Thinking

author.name: Mete Ismayilzada, Simone A. Luchini, Abdulkadir Gokce, Badr AlKhamissi, Antoine Bosselut, Antonio Laverghetta Jr., Lonneke van der Plas, Roger E. Beaty

entry.summary: Investigates brain-LLM alignment during creative thinking using fMRI data from 170 participants performing the Alternate Uses Task. Finds that LLMs with higher divergent thinking performance show greater alignment with brain regions associated with creativity.

entry.title: Testing the Limits of Truth Directions in LLMs

author.name: Angelos Poulis, Mark Crovella, Evimaria Terzi

entry.summary: Identifies key limits of truth direction universality in LLMs: truth directions are layer-dependent, task-type dependent (factual vs reasoning), and topic-dependent. Provides nuanced picture beyond prior binary claims.

entry.title: Relative Density Ratio Optimization for Stable and Statistically Consistent Model Alignment

author.name: Hiroshi Takahashi, Tomoharu Iwata, Atsutoshi Kumagai, Sekitoshi Kanai, Masanori Yamada, Kosuke Nishida, Kazutoshi Shinoda

entry.summary: Proposes relative density ratio optimization for LLM alignment that achieves statistical consistency without assuming specific preference models like Bradley-Terry, offering more stable training than direct density ratio optimization.

entry.title: AI Agents Under EU Law

author.name: Luca Nannini, Adam Leon Smith, Michele Joshua Maggini, Enrico Panai, Sandra Feliciano, Aleksandr Tiulkanov, Elena Maran, James Gealy, Piercosma Bisconti

entry.summary: First systematic regulatory mapping of AI agents under EU law, covering AI Act, GDPR, Cyber Resilience Act, and other regulations, analyzing compliance requirements across the agent lifecycle.

entry.title: The Role of Generator Access in Autoregressive Post-Training

author.name: Amit Kiran Rege

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of how generator access interfaces constrain autoregressive post-training, showing that root-start sampling limits all observation types to one canonical experiment, while weak prefix control creates exponential capability gaps.

entry.title: Emergent Compositional Communication for Latent World Properties

author.name: Tomek Kaszy\'nski

entry.summary: Shows that multi-agent communication pressure can extract discrete, compositional representations of invisible physical properties (elasticity, friction, mass) from frozen video features via Gumbel-Softmax bottleneck with iterated learning. Achieves near-perfect compositionality.

entry.title: Beyond Few-Step Inference: Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformer Model Serving with Inter-Request Caching Reuse

author.name: Hao Liu, Ye Huang, Chenghuan Huang, Zhenyi Zheng, Jiangsu Du, Ziyang Ma, Jing Lyu, Yutong Lu

entry.summary: Chorus accelerates video diffusion transformer serving by caching and reusing features across different requests, achieving up to 45% speedup even on 4-step distilled models where intra-request caching is ineffective. Uses a three-stage caching strategy.

entry.title: LoMa: Local Feature Matching Revisited

author.name: David Nordstr\"om, Johan Edstedt, Georg B\"okman, Jonathan Astermark, Anders Heyden, Viktor Larsson, M{\aa}rten Wadenb\"ack, Michael Felsberg, Fredrik Kahl

entry.summary: LoMa revisits local feature matching from a data-driven perspective, combining large diverse data mixtures, modern training recipes, and scaled compute to achieve remarkable gains, suggesting the field has been data-limited rather than architecture-limited.

entry.title: TableVision: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Spatially Grounded Reasoning over Complex Hierarchical Tables

author.name: Xiaoyu Chen, Lu Dai, Hanqing Wang, Zhuoyu Li, Wenbin Dai, Yanzong Zheng, Zhenggang Xia, Junyong Lin, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Introduces TableVision, a large-scale benchmark for spatially grounded reasoning over complex hierarchical tables by MLLMs, identifying a 'Perceptual Overload' bottleneck where models struggle with increasing visual complexity.

entry.title: SKILLFOUNDRY: Building Self-Evolving Agent Skill Libraries from Heterogeneous Scientific Resources

author.name: Shuaike Shen, Wenduo Cheng, Mingqian Ma, Alistair Turcan, Martin Jinye Zhang, Jian Ma

entry.summary: Presents SkillFoundry, a self-evolving framework that converts heterogeneous scientific resources (APIs, scripts, papers, etc.) into validated, reusable agent skills organized via a domain knowledge tree.

entry.title: Comparative reversal learning reveals rigid adaptation in LLMs under non-stationary uncertainty

author.name: Haomiaomiao Wang, Tom\'as E Ward, Lili Zhang

entry.summary: Tests LLMs (DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3, GPT-5.2) on probabilistic reversal learning tasks, finding rigid adaptation patterns with strong win-stay but weak lose-shift behavior, revealing fundamental limitations in non-stationary decision-making.

entry.title: TimeSeek: Temporal Reliability of Agentic Forecasters

author.name: Hamza Mostafa, Om Shastri, Dennis Lee

entry.summary: Introduces TimeSeek, a benchmark evaluating 10 frontier LLM forecasters on 150 Kalshi prediction markets at five temporal checkpoints. Models are most competitive early and on uncertain markets; web search helps on average but hurts in 12% of cases.

entry.title: REAM: Merging Improves Pruning of Experts in LLMs

author.name: Saurav Jha, Maryam Hashemzadeh, Ali Saheb Pasand, Ali Parviz, Min-Joong Lee, Boris Knyazev

entry.summary: Proposes REAM (Router-weighted Expert Activation Merging) for compressing MoE LLMs by merging (rather than pruning) expert groups, better preserving performance. Evaluated across multiple MoE models and benchmarks.

entry.title: Incompleteness of AI Safety Verification via Kolmogorov Complexity

author.name: Munawar Hasan

entry.summary: Proves an incompleteness result for AI safety verification using Kolmogorov complexity: for any sound verifier, there exists a complexity threshold beyond which true policy-compliant instances cannot be certified, establishing fundamental limits on formal verification.

entry.title: V-Reflection: Transforming MLLMs from Passive Observers to Active Interrogators

author.name: Jiazhou Zhou, Yucheng Chen, Hongyang Li, Qing Jiang, Hu Zhou, Ying-Cong Chen, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes V-Reflection, a framework transforming MLLMs from passive observers to active interrogators through a 'think-then-look' mechanism where reasoning latent states function as dynamic probes that actively re-examine visual details.

entry.title: Evolutionary Search for Automated Design of Uncertainty Quantification Methods

author.name: Mikhail Seleznyov, Daniil Korbut, Viktor Moskvoretskii, Oleg Somov, Alexander Panchenko, Elena Tutubalina

entry.summary: Uses LLM-powered evolutionary search to automatically discover uncertainty quantification methods for LLMs, represented as Python programs. Evolved methods outperform hand-designed baselines by up to 6.7% ROC-AUC across 9 datasets.

entry.title: Automated Conjecture Resolution with Formal Verification

author.name: Haocheng Ju, Guoxiong Gao, Jiedong Jiang, Bin Wu, Zeming Sun, Leheng Chen, Yutong Wang, Yuefeng Wang, Zichen Wang, Wanyi He, Peihao Wu, Liang Xiao, Ruochuan Liu, Bryan Dai, Bin Dong

entry.summary: Proposes an automated framework combining informal reasoning (Rethlas) and formal verification (Archon) agents for tackling research-level math problems end-to-end with minimal human intervention.

entry.title: TraceGuard: Structured Multi-Dimensional Monitoring as a Collusion-Resistant Control Protocol

author.name: Khanh Linh Nguyen, Hoa Nghiem, Tu Tran

entry.summary: TraceGuard is a structured multi-dimensional monitoring protocol for AI control that evaluates agent actions across five dimensions to detect attacks, specifically addressing collusion where monitor and agent are the same model.

entry.title: APPA: Adaptive Preference Pluralistic Alignment for Fair Federated RLHF of LLMs

author.name: Mahmoud Srewa, Tianyu Zhao, Salma Elmalaki

entry.summary: Proposes APPA, a federated RLHF framework that dynamically reweights group rewards to achieve fair pluralistic alignment of LLMs with diverse preferences without centralizing data.

entry.title: Responses Fall Short of Understanding: Revealing the Gap between Internal Representations and Responses in Visual Document Understanding

author.name: Haruka Kawasaki, Ryota Tanaka, Kyosuke Nishida

entry.summary: Reveals a gap between internal representations and generated responses in visual document understanding - LVLMs often have correct information internally but fail to generate correct answers, with information being present earlier in the network.

entry.title: SLaB: Sparse-Lowrank-Binary Decomposition for Efficient Large Language Models

author.name: Ziwei Li, Yuang Ma, Yi Kang

entry.summary: SLaB decomposes LLM weight matrices into sparse + low-rank + binary components without retraining, reducing perplexity by up to 48% compared to existing methods at high compression ratios.

entry.title: What Makes Good Multilingual Reasoning? Disentangling Reasoning Traces with Measurable Features

author.name: Dayeon Ki, Kevin Duh, Marine Carpuat

entry.summary: Investigates what characterizes effective multilingual reasoning in LRMs, defining measurable features of reasoning traces and using logistic regression and sparse autoencoders to analyze them across languages.

entry.title: Rethinking Exploration in RLVR: From Entropy Regularization to Refinement via Bidirectional Entropy Modulation

author.name: Hengrui Gu, Xiaotian Han, Yujing Bian, Kaixiong Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes bidirectional entropy modulation for RLVR that decomposes policy entropy into 'exploration entropy' and 'refinement entropy,' enabling targeted control rather than blanket entropy regularization. Shows improved reasoning performance.

entry.title: Correcting Source Mismatch in Flow Matching with Radial-Angular Transport

author.name: Fouad Oubari, Mathilde Mougeot

entry.summary: Introduces Radial-Angular Flow Matching (RAFM), which corrects source mismatch in flow matching by matching the radial distribution of the source to the data and reducing the transport problem to angular alignment on spheres. This addresses a known limitation of Gaussian sources for heavy-tailed data.

entry.title: Learning from Equivalence Queries, Revisited

author.name: Mark Braverman, Roi Livni, Yishay Mansour, Shay Moran, Kobbi Nissim

entry.summary: Revisits Angluin's classical model of learning from equivalence queries with modern motivations (generative models, recommendation systems). Introduces relaxed counterexample models and partial-information settings beyond the fully adversarial, full-information case.

entry.title: Data Attribution in Adaptive Learning

author.name: Amit Kiran Rege

entry.summary: Formalizes occurrence-level data attribution for adaptive learning systems where training data is self-generated (online bandits, RL, LLM post-training), proving that replay-side information cannot recover attribution in general while identifying tractable structural classes.

entry.title: Physics-Constrained Adaptive Flow Matching for Climate Downscaling

author.name: Kevin Debeire, Ayta\c{c} Pa\c{c}al, Pierre Gentine, Luis Medrano-Navarro, Nils Thuerey, Veronika Eyring

entry.summary: Presents Physics-Constrained Adaptive Flow Matching (PC-AFM) for climate downscaling, adding soft conservation constraints for precipitation and humidity and gradient-guided conditioning for out-of-distribution generalization under climate change scenarios.

entry.title: Shorter, but Still Trustworthy? An Empirical Study of Chain-of-Thought Compression

author.name: Lingjie Zeng, Xiaofan Chen, Yanbo Wang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: Conducts the first systematic study of how Chain-of-Thought compression affects model trustworthiness (safety, hallucination resistance, multilingual robustness), finding that CoT compression can degrade trustworthiness even when accuracy is preserved.

entry.title: When Sinks Help or Hurt: Unified Framework for Attention Sink in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiho Choi, Jaemin Kim, Sanghwan Kim, Seunghoon Hong, Jin-Hwi Park

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework categorizing attention sinks in Large Vision-Language Models into ViT-emerged (V-sinks) and LLM-emerged (L-sinks). Reveals a fundamental performance trade-off where sinks encode global priors but suppress fine-grained visual evidence. Provides new understanding of attention mechanisms in multimodal models.

entry.title: 1.x-Distill: Breaking the Diversity, Quality, and Efficiency Barrier in Distribution Matching Distillation

author.name: Haoyu Li, Tingyan Wen, Lin Qi, Zhe Wu, Yihuang Chen, Xing Zhou, Lifei Zhu, Xueqian Wang, Kai Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes 1.x-Distill, the first fractional-step distillation framework for diffusion models breaking the integer-step constraint. Analyzes the overlooked role of teacher CFG in Distribution Matching Distillation and introduces modifications to suppress mode collapse. Establishes 1.x-step generation as a practical regime.

entry.title: AURA: Always-On Understanding and Real-Time Assistance via Video Streams

author.name: Xudong Lu, Yang Bo, Jinpeng Chen, Shuhan Li, Xintong Guo, Huankang Guan, Fang Liu, Dunyuan Xu, Peiwen Sun, Heyang Sun, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: AURA is an end-to-end streaming visual interaction framework that enables VideoLLMs to continuously process live video streams for real-time question answering and proactive assistance, going beyond offline video understanding.

entry.title: Graph-to-Frame RAG: Visual-Space Knowledge Fusion for Training-Free and Auditable Video Reasoning

author.name: Songyuan Yang, Weijiang Yu, Ziyu Liu, Guijian Tang, Wenjing Yang, Huibin Tan, Nong Xiao

entry.summary: G2F-RAG delivers external knowledge to video reasoning models in the visual space by rendering knowledge graph information directly onto video frames, rather than appending text. Training-free and auditable approach that avoids attention dilution.

entry.title: The Blind Spot of Adaptation: Quantifying and Mitigating Forgetting in Fine-tuned Driving Models

author.name: Runhao Mao, Hanshi Wang, Yixiang Yang, Qianli Ma, Jingmeng Zhou, Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: First systematic investigation of catastrophic forgetting in fine-tuned autonomous driving VLMs, introducing a 180K scene dataset for benchmarking forgetting and revealing that existing methods suffer significant knowledge erosion.

entry.title: Beyond the Global Scores: Fine-Grained Token Grounding as a Robust Detector of LVLM Hallucinations

author.name: Tuan Dung Nguyen, Minh Khoi Ho, Qi Chen, Yutong Xie, Nguyen Cam-Tu, Minh Khoi Nguyen, Dang Huy Pham Nguyen, Anton van den Hengel, Johan W. Verjans, Phi Le Nguyen, Vu Minh Hieu Phan

entry.summary: Proposes patch-level hallucination detection for LVLMs, observing that faithful object tokens must be strongly grounded in specific image regions rather than having weak scattered correlations that aggregate into deceptively high global relevance.

entry.title: Free-Range Gaussians: Non-Grid-Aligned Generative 3D Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Ahan Shabanov, Peter Hedman, Ethan Weber, Zhengqin Li, Denis Rozumny, Gael Le Lan, Naina Dhingra, Lei Luo, Andrea Vedaldi, Christian Richardt, Andrea Tagliasacchi, Bo Zhu, Numair Khan

entry.summary: Free-Range Gaussians predicts non-grid-aligned 3D Gaussians from as few as four images using flow matching, avoiding the redundancy of pixel/voxel-aligned approaches and synthesizing plausible content in unobserved regions.

entry.title: AgenticFlict: A Large-Scale Dataset of Merge Conflicts in AI Coding Agent Pull Requests on GitHub

author.name: Daniel Ogenrwot, John Businge

entry.summary: AgenticFlict presents a large-scale dataset of 142K+ AI coding agent pull requests from 59K+ repos, focusing on merge conflicts in AI-generated contributions. First large-scale study of integration challenges with AI coding agents.

entry.title: TriAttention: Efficient Long Reasoning with Trigonometric KV Compression

author.name: Weian Mao, Xi Lin, Wei Huang, Yuxin Xie, Tianfu Fu, Bohan Zhuang, Song Han, Yukang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes TriAttention for KV cache compression in long reasoning, discovering that pre-RoPE Q/K vectors concentrate around stable centers, enabling a trigonometric importance estimation that avoids post-RoPE query rotation issues.

entry.title: Focus Matters: Phase-Aware Suppression for Hallucination in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sohyeon Kim, Sang Yeon Yoon, Kyeongbo Kong

entry.summary: Identifies a three-phase attention structure (diffusion, focus, rediffusion) in vision encoders of LVLMs and proposes phase-aware suppression to reduce hallucinations without iterative optimization overhead.

entry.title: DRAFT: Task Decoupled Latent Reasoning for Agent Safety

author.name: Lin Wang, Junfeng Fang, Dan Zhang, Fei Shen, Xiang Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: DRAFT proposes a latent reasoning framework for agent safety that decouples safety judgment into an Extractor (trajectory to latent draft) and Reasoner (safety prediction), avoiding lossy explicit summarization for safety monitoring of tool-using agents.

entry.title: Benchmarking Multi-turn Medical Diagnosis: Hold, Lure, and Self-Correction

author.name: Jinrui Fang, Runhan Chen, Xu Yang, Jian Yu, Jiawei Xu, Ashwin Vinod, Wenqi Shi, Tianlong Chen, Heng Ji, ChengXiang Zhai, Ying Ding, Yuji Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MINT, a multi-turn medical diagnosis benchmark with 1,035 cases and clinically labeled evidence shards, revealing three problematic LLM behaviors: premature answering (55%+), susceptibility to misleading evidence, and poor self-correction.

entry.title: VERT: Reliable LLM Judges for Radiology Report Evaluation

author.name: Federica Bologna, Jean-Philippe Corbeil, Matthew Wilkens, Asma Ben Abacha

entry.summary: Proposes VERT, an LLM-based metric for evaluating radiology reports, and conducts thorough correlation analysis with expert ratings across multiple modalities and anatomies. Compares against existing metrics like RadFact and GREEN.

entry.title: Explainable Model Routing for Agentic Workflows

author.name: Mika Okamoto, Ansel Kaplan Erol, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: Introduces Topaz, a framework for explainable model routing in agentic workflows that replaces silent model assignments with interpretable routing decisions including skill profiling, capability-cost frontiers, and audit traces. From Mark Riedl's group.

entry.title: Decomposing Communication Gain and Delay Cost Under Cross-Timestep Delays in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zihong Gao, Hongjian Liang, Lei Hao, Liangjun Ke

entry.summary: Formalizes cross-timestep communication delays in cooperative MARL as DeComm-POMG, decomposes message effects into communication gain and delay cost, and establishes value-loss bounds for delayed messages.

entry.title: FeynmanBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs on Diagrammatic Physics Reasoning

author.name: Zeyu Wang, Xiaogang Li, Peiyao Xiao, Qinhao Kong, Ben Wang, Chengliang Xu, Zichao Chen, Bing Zhao, Hu Wei

entry.summary: Introduces FeynmanBench, the first benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on Feynman diagram tasks requiring conservation laws, symmetry constraints, graph topology identification, and algebraic conversion.

entry.title: RESCORE: LLM-Driven Simulation Recovery in Control Systems Research Papers

author.name: Vineet Bhat, Shiqing Wei, Ali Umut Kaypak, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Ramesh Karri, Farshad Khorrami

entry.summary: Defines Paper-to-Simulation Recoverability and proposes RESCORE, a three-component LLM framework for reconstructing numerical simulations from control systems papers. Achieves 40.7% recovery rate on 500 CDC papers.

entry.title: RoboPhD: Evolving Diverse Complex Agents Under Tight Evaluation Budgets

author.name: Andrew Borthwick, Stephen Ash, Anthony Galczak

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic comparison of optimization paradigms for LLM-guided agent evolution under tight evaluation budgets: Elo tournament selection, Pareto-based selection, and greedy hill-climbing.

entry.title: Automatically Generating Hard Math Problems from Hypothesis-Driven Error Analysis

author.name: Jiayu Fu, Mourad Heddaya, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: Proposes a pipeline for automatically generating hard math benchmark problems using AI-generated hypotheses about LLM weaknesses, then targeting those specific concept/skill gaps.

entry.title: Search, Do not Guess: Teaching Small Language Models to Be Effective Search Agents

author.name: Yizhou Liu, Qi Sun, Yulin Chen, Siyue Zhang, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: Demonstrates that small language models (SLMs) invoke search tools less frequently than LLMs and are more prone to hallucination, then proposes a lightweight fine-tuning approach to train SLMs to reliably retrieve and generate grounded answers for multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: SoLA: Leveraging Soft Activation Sparsity and Low-Rank Decomposition for Large Language Model Compression

author.name: Xinhao Huang, You-Liang Huang, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: Proposes SoLA, a training-free LLM compression method that combines soft activation sparsity analysis with low-rank decomposition, identifying components that contribute significantly to inference and compressing the rest.

entry.title: AIFS-COMPO: A Global Data-Driven Atmospheric Composition Forecasting System

author.name: Paula Harder, Johannes Flemming, Mihai Alexe, Gert Mertes, Baudouin Raoult, Matthew Chantry

entry.summary: Introduces AIFS-COMPO, a transformer-based model from ECMWF for global atmospheric composition forecasting that jointly models meteorological and chemical variables, achieving competitive performance with the operational CAMS system at lower cost.

entry.title: Measuring LLM Trust Allocation Across Conflicting Software Artifacts

author.name: Noshin Ulfat, Ahsanul Ameen Sabit, Soneya Binta Hossain

entry.summary: Presents TRACE framework for measuring how LLMs allocate trust across conflicting software artifacts (code, docs, tests), using 22,339 traces from seven models to evaluate per-artifact quality assessment and trust calibration.

entry.title: Sim2Real-AD: A Modular Sim-to-Real Framework for Deploying VLM-Guided Reinforcement Learning in Real-World Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zilin Huang, Zhengyang Wan, Zihao Sheng, Boyue Wang, Junwei You, Yue Leng, Sikai Chen

entry.summary: Sim2Real-AD presents a modular framework for zero-shot transfer of VLM-guided RL policies trained in CARLA simulation to real autonomous vehicles. Decomposes the transfer into four components including geometric observation bridging and physics-aware action mapping.

entry.title: Inside the Scaffold: A Source-Code Taxonomy of Coding Agent Architectures

author.name: Benjamin Rombaut

entry.summary: Presents a source-code-level architectural taxonomy of 13 open-source coding agent scaffolds, characterizing them across 12 dimensions including control loops, tool definitions, state management, and context strategy.

entry.title: Unveiling Language Routing Isolation in Multilingual MoE Models for Interpretable Subnetwork Adaptation

author.name: Kening Zheng, Wei-Chieh Huang, Jiahao Huo, Zhonghao Li, Henry Peng Zou, Yibo Yan, Xin Zou, Jungang Li, Junzhuo Li, Hanrong Zhang, Xuming Hu, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Reveals Language Routing Isolation in MoE models where high- and low-resource languages activate disjoint expert sets. Proposes RISE framework to exploit this for targeted language-specific adaptation.

entry.title: Unlocking Prompt Infilling Capability for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yoshinari Fujinuma, Keisuke Sakaguchi

entry.summary: Shows that extending full-sequence masking during SFT of diffusion language models unlocks prompt infilling capability. Model-infilled prompts match or surpass manually designed templates.

entry.title: I-CALM: Incentivizing Confidence-Aware Abstention for LLM Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Haotian Zong, Binze Li, Yufei Long, Sinyin Chang, Jialong Wu, Gillian K. Hadfield

entry.summary: I-CALM studies whether prompt-only interventions with explicit reward schemes for answer-vs-abstain decisions can reduce LLM hallucination, incentivizing confidence-aware abstention.

entry.title: BAAI Cardiac Agent: An intelligent multimodal agent for automated reasoning and diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging

author.name: Taiping Qu, Hongkai Zhang, Lantian Zhang, Can Zhao, Nan Zhang, Hui Wang, Zhen Zhou, Mingye Zou, Kairui Bo, Pengfei Zhao, Xingxing Jin, Zixian Su, Kun Jiang, Huan Liu, Yu Du, Maozhou Wang, Ruifang Yan, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Lei Xu, Henggui Zhang

entry.summary: BAAI Cardiac Agent is a multimodal AI system for end-to-end cardiac MRI interpretation, integrating segmentation, functional quantification, tissue characterization, and structured report generation. Evaluated on 2,413 patients.

entry.title: GENFIG1: Visual Summaries of Scholarly Work as a Challenge for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yaohan Guan, Pristina Wang, Najim Dehak, Alan Yuille, Jieneng Chen, Daniel Khashabi

entry.summary: Introduces GENFIG1, a benchmark evaluating VLMs on generating 'Figure 1'-style visual summaries of research papers, requiring scientific reasoning coupled with visual communication skills.

entry.title: Which English Do LLMs Prefer? Triangulating Structural Bias Towards American English in Foundation Models

author.name: Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Davood Rafiei

entry.summary: Investigates structural bias in LLMs toward American English over British English using a curated corpus of 1,813 variants and a new DiAlign method for measuring dialectal alignment, finding systematic AmE preference across models.

entry.title: Effects of Generative AI Errors on User Reliance Across Task Difficulty

author.name: Jacy Reese Anthis, Hannah Cha, Solon Barocas, Alexandra Chouldechova, Jake Hofman

entry.summary: Preregistered experiment (N=577) studying how generative AI errors affect user reliance, finding that easy-task errors don't reduce use more than hard-task errors, challenging the 'jagged frontier' concern.

entry.title: DP-OPD: Differentially Private On-Policy Distillation for Language Models

author.name: Fatemeh Khadem, Sajad Mousavi, Yi Fang, Yuhong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DP-OPD, a differentially private distillation method for LLMs that applies DP only to the teacher and uses on-policy distillation to avoid exposure bias in the student.

entry.title: One Model for All: Multi-Objective Controllable Language Models

author.name: Qiang He, Yucheng Yang, Tianyi Zhou, Meng Fang, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Setareh Maghsudi

entry.summary: Proposes training one LLM that can be controlled at inference to satisfy different users' multi-objective preferences, combining multi-objective RLHF with controllable generation.

entry.title: Multilingual Prompt Localization for Agent-as-a-Judge: Language and Backbone Sensitivity in Requirement-Level Evaluation

author.name: Alhasan Mahmood, Samir Abdaljalil, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Shows that changing the evaluation language of Agent-as-a-Judge prompts can invert backbone rankings across LLMs, with no single model dominating all languages across 4,950 judge runs.

entry.title: StableTTA: Training-Free Test-Time Adaptation that Improves Model Accuracy on ImageNet1K to 96%

author.name: Zheng Li, Jerry Cheng, Huanying Helen Gu

entry.summary: StableTTA is a training-free test-time adaptation method achieving 96% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K, enabling lightweight models to outperform ViT while using <5% parameters.

entry.title: PassiveQA: A Three-Action Framework for Epistemically Calibrated Question Answering via Supervised Finetuning

author.name: Madhav S Baidya

entry.summary: Proposes PassiveQA, a framework where LLMs must decide whether to Answer, Ask for clarification, or Abstain, addressing the problem of overconfident responses to incomplete queries.

entry.title: Training-Free Refinement of Flow Matching with Divergence-based Sampling

author.name: Yeonwoo Cha, Jaehoon Yoo, Semin Kim, Yunseo Park, Jinhyeon Kwon, Seunghoon Hong

entry.summary: Proposes Flow Divergence Sampler (FDS), a training-free method that refines intermediate states during flow matching inference by quantifying velocity field misguidance through divergence computation.

entry.title: Discovering Failure Modes in Vision-Language Models using RL

author.name: Kanishk Jain, Qian Yang, Shravan Nayak, Parisa Kordjamshidi, Nishanth Anand, Aishwarya Agrawal

entry.summary: Proposes an RL-based framework to automatically discover failure modes and blind spots in Vision-Language Models, replacing costly manual identification of weaknesses like counting and spatial reasoning errors.

entry.title: A Bayesian Information-Theoretic Approach to Data Attribution

author.name: Dharmesh Tailor, Nicol\`o Felicioni, Kamil Ciosek

entry.summary: Formulates training data attribution as Bayesian information-theoretic problem, scoring subsets by information loss (entropy increase when removed). Scales using GP surrogates built from tangent features.

entry.title: Where to Steer: Input-Dependent Layer Selection for Steering Improves LLM Alignment

author.name: Soham Gadgil, Chris Lin, Su-In Lee

entry.summary: Proposes input-dependent layer selection for steering vectors in LLMs, showing theoretically and empirically that the optimal intervention layer varies across inputs, and adaptive selection improves alignment.

entry.title: The Geometric Alignment Tax: Tokenization vs. Continuous Geometry in Scientific Foundation Models

author.name: Prashant C. Raju

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Geometric Alignment Tax'—the cost of forcing continuous manifolds through discrete categorical bottlenecks in scientific foundation models. Shows continuous heads reduce geometric distortion by up to 8.5x.

entry.title: Which Leakage Types Matter?

author.name: Simon Roth

entry.summary: Comprehensive study of four data leakage classes across 2,047 datasets, finding that normalization leakage (Class I) is negligible while selection leakage (Class II) is substantial, inverting the textbook emphasis.

entry.title: Towards Unveiling Vulnerabilities of Large Reasoning Models in Machine Unlearning

author.name: Aobo Chen, Chenxu Zhao, Chenglin Miao, Mengdi Huai

entry.summary: Proposes the first unlearning attack specifically targeting large reasoning models (LRMs), exploiting how unlearning creates new security vulnerabilities in models with explicit multi-step reasoning traces.

entry.title: FlashSAC: Fast and Stable Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Robot Control

author.name: Donghu Kim, Youngdo Lee, Minho Park, Kinam Kim, I Made Aswin Nahendra, Takuma Seno, Sehee Min, Daniel Palenicek, Florian Vogt, Danica Kragic, Jan Peters, Jaegul Choo, Hojoon Lee

entry.summary: Presents FlashSAC, a fast and stable off-policy RL algorithm built on SAC that addresses slow convergence and instability in high-dimensional robot control. Motivated by scaling laws for critic learning to balance convergence speed and stability.

entry.title: Nonparametric Regression Discontinuity Designs with Survival Outcomes

author.name: Maximilian Schuessler, Erik Sverdrup, Robert Tibshirani, Stefan Wager

entry.summary: Proposes nonparametric regression discontinuity design methods for survival outcomes with censoring, combining doubly robust censoring correction with local polynomial regression. Led by Wager and Tibshirani (Stanford).

entry.title: Rethinking Token Prediction: Tree-Structured Diffusion Language Model

author.name: Zihao Wu, Haoming Yang, Juncheng Dong, Vahid Tarokh

entry.summary: Proposes a tree-structured diffusion language model that replaces the full-vocabulary prediction layer (>20% of parameters) with a hierarchical tree structure, reducing parameter count and memory usage while maintaining performance.

entry.title: On the Efficiency of Sinkhorn-Knopp for Entropically Regularized Optimal Transport

author.name: Kun He

entry.summary: Resolves a theory-practice gap for the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm by introducing 'well-boundedness,' a local property that isolates well-behaved portions of the transport plan from outlier-affected regions, yielding tighter convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Topological Sensitivity in Connectome-Constrained Neural Networks

author.name: Nalin Dhiman

entry.summary: Investigates topological sensitivity of connectome-constrained neural networks, showing that the apparent advantage of biological graph topology over random controls largely disappears under stricter experimental controls (shared initialization, degree-preserving rewiring).

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Integrity for Modern Neural Networks: Structured Drift Proofs via Norm, Rank, and Sparsity Certificates

author.name: Zhenhang Shang, Kani Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Fine-Tuning Integrity (FTI) as a security goal and Succinct Model Difference Proofs (SMDPs) as zero-knowledge proofs certifying that fine-tuned models differ from base models only within policy-defined drift constraints on norm, rank, and sparsity.

entry.title: Researchers waste 80% of LLM annotation costs by classifying one text at a time

author.name: Christian Pipal, Eva-Maria Vogel, Morgan Wack, Frank Esser

entry.summary: Demonstrates that batching 25 items and stacking multiple variables into single LLM prompts reduces annotation costs by 80%+ while maintaining accuracy within 2pp for 6/8 models. Tests up to batch size 1000 across 8 production LLMs.

entry.title: CoLA: Cross-Modal Low-rank Adaptation for Multimodal Downstream Tasks

author.name: Wish Suharitdamrong, Tony Alex, Muhammad Awais, Sara Ahmed

entry.summary: Proposes Cross-Modal Low-rank Adaptation (CoLA), extending LoRA with a dedicated inter-modal adaptation pathway for multimodal tasks using dual-stream architectures like DINO+BERT. Introduces both intra-modal and inter-modal adaptation paths for better cross-modal interaction capture. Addresses a genuine gap in parameter-efficient fine-tuning for multimodal settings.

entry.title: A Systematic Study of Cross-Modal Typographic Attacks on Audio-Visual Reasoning

author.name: Tianle Chen, Deepti Ghadiyaram

entry.summary: Systematically studies cross-modal typographic attacks on audio-visual MLLMs, finding coordinated multi-modal attacks far more potent (83.43% vs 34.93% success rate) than single-modality attacks. Tests multiple frontier MLLMs across various tasks. Important security finding.

entry.title: ATSS: Detecting AI-Generated Videos via Anomalous Temporal Self-Similarity

author.name: Hang Wang, Chao Shen, Lei Zhang, Zhi-Qi Cheng

entry.summary: Identifies anomalous temporal self-similarity (ATSS) as a distinctive fingerprint of AI-generated videos, where AIGVs show unnaturally repetitive correlations from deterministic anchor-driven trajectories. Proposes a multimodal detection method exploiting this signal. Novel forensic insight into AI video generation.

entry.title: DriveVA: Video Action Models are Zero-Shot Drivers

author.name: Mengmeng Liu, Diankun Zhang, Jiuming Liu, Jianfeng Cui, Hongwei Xie, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Michael Ying Yang, Francesco Nex, Hao Cheng

entry.summary: DriveVA is an autonomous driving world model that jointly decodes future visual forecasts and action sequences in a shared latent generative process, inheriting rich priors from video action models for zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Reinforce to Learn, Elect to Reason: A Dual Paradigm for Video Reasoning

author.name: Songyuan Yang, Weijiang Yu, Jilin Ma, Ziyu Liu, Guijian Tang, Wenjing Yang, Huibin Tan, Nong Xiao

entry.summary: RLER introduces a dual paradigm for video reasoning that decouples learning to produce evidence from obtaining reliable answers, using group-relative RL with novel task-driven rewards including frame-sensitive, think-transparency, and anti-repetition rewards.

entry.title: Erasure or Erosion? Evaluating Compositional Degradation in Unlearned Text-To-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Arian Komaei Koma, Seyed Amir Kasaei, Ali Aghayari, AmirMahdi Sadeghzadeh, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models through the lens of compositional generation, revealing consistent trade-offs between unlearning effectiveness and compositional integrity.

entry.title: OpenWorldLib: A Unified Codebase and Definition of Advanced World Models

author.name: DataFlow Team, Bohan Zeng, Daili Hua, Kaixin Zhu, Yifan Dai, Bozhou Li, Yuran Wang, Chengzhuo Tong, Yifan Yang, Mingkun Chang, Jianbin Zhao, Zhou Liu, Hao Liang, Xiaochen Ma, Ruichuan An, Junbo Niu, Zimo Meng, Tianyi Bai, Meiyi Qiang, Huanyao Zhang, Zhiyou Xiao, Tianyu Guo, Qinhan Yu, Runhao Zhao, Zhengpin Li, Xinyi Huang, Yisheng Pan, Yiwen Tang, Yang Shi, Yue Ding, Xinlong Chen, Hongcheng Gao, Minglei Shi, Jialong Wu, Zekun Wang, Yuanxing Zhang, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Yiren Song, Mike Zheng Shou, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: OpenWorldLib provides a unified definition and standardized inference framework for 'Advanced World Models,' proposing that world models are perception-centered with interaction and long-term memory capabilities. Integrates multiple model types into a common framework.

entry.title: CLEAR: Unlocking Generative Potential for Degraded Image Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Xiangzhao Hao, Zefeng Zhang, Zhenyu Zhang, Linhao Yu, Yao Chen, Yiqian Zhang, Haiyun Guo, Shuohuan Wang, Yu Sun

entry.summary: CLEAR connects the understanding and generation pathways of unified multimodal models to handle degraded image inputs, addressing the disconnect where models fail to leverage their generative capacity for restoration during reasoning.

entry.title: From Prompt to Physical Action: Structured Backdoor Attacks on LLM-Mediated Robotic Control Systems

author.name: Mingyang Xie, Jin Wei-Kocsis

entry.summary: Investigates structured backdoor attacks on LLM-mediated ROS2 robotic control systems via LoRA-based supply-chain poisoning. Finds that backdoors at the natural-language reasoning stage don't reliably propagate to executable robot commands, revealing important insights about pipeline vulnerability.

entry.title: Persistent Cross-Attempt State Optimization for Repository-Level Code Generation

author.name: Ruwei Pan, Jiangshuai Wang, Qisheng Zhang, Yueheng Zhu, Linhao Wu, Zixiong Yang, Yakun Zhang, Lu Zhang, Hongyu Zhang

entry.summary: LiveCoder maintains persistent task-specific state across multiple code generation attempts, capturing success/failure knowledge to guide subsequent repository-level code generation.

entry.title: Do No Harm: Exposing Hidden Vulnerabilities of LLMs via Persona-based Client Simulation Attack in Psychological Counseling

author.name: Qingyang Xu, Yaling Shen, Stephanie Fong, Zimu Wang, Yiwen Jiang, Xiangyu Zhao, Jiahe Liu, Zhongxing Xu, Vincent Lee, Zongyuan Ge

entry.summary: Introduces PCSA, the first red-teaming framework for psychological counseling LLMs that simulates persona-driven client dialogues to expose safety vulnerabilities where therapeutic empathy may reinforce harmful beliefs in multi-turn conversations.

entry.title: IC3-Evolve: Proof-/Witness-Gated Offline LLM-Driven Heuristic Evolution for IC3 Hardware Model Checking

author.name: Mingkai Miao, Guangyu Hu, Ziyi Yang, Hongce Zhang

entry.summary: IC3-Evolve uses LLMs to automatically propose and validate small patches to IC3 hardware model checking heuristics, with proof/witness gating to ensure correctness. This bridges LLM code generation with formal verification, ensuring every candidate patch is auditable.

entry.title: TABQAWORLD: Optimizing Multimodal Reasoning for Multi-Turn Table Question Answering

author.name: Tung Sum Thomas Kwok, Xinyu Wang, Xiaofeng Lin, Peng Lu, Chunhe Wang, Changlun Li, Hanwei Wu, Nan Tang, Elisa Kreiss, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces TABQAWORLD, a framework for multi-turn table question answering that optimizes tabular action through representation and estimation, addressing error accumulation in text serialization of tables over multiple reasoning turns.

entry.title: GUIDE: Interpretable GUI Agent Evaluation via Hierarchical Diagnosis

author.name: Yuwen Zhai, Runze Li, Liang Wang, Nian Shi, Liwu Xu, Wei Zhang, Ran Lin, Bo Xu, Benlei Cui

entry.summary: Introduces GUIDE, a hierarchical diagnostic evaluation framework for GUI agents that decomposes trajectory assessment into segmentation, summarization, and scoring stages for interpretable evaluation.

entry.title: Receding-Horizon Control via Drifting Models

author.name: Daniele Foffano, Alessio Russo, Alexandre Proutiere

entry.summary: Proposes Drifting MPC, an offline trajectory optimization framework that combines drifting generative models with receding-horizon planning for systems with unknown dynamics, learning conditional trajectory distributions from offline datasets.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence and Systemic Risk: A Unified Model of Performative Prediction, Algorithmic Herding, and Cognitive Dependency in Financial Markets

author.name: Shuchen Meng, Xupeng Chen

entry.summary: Develops a unified model showing AI adoption in financial markets generates systemic risk through three reinforcing channels: performative prediction, algorithmic herding, and cognitive dependency, with a convex coupling that grows superlinearly with adoption.

entry.title: Scaling Teams or Scaling Time? Memory Enabled Lifelong Learning in LLM Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Shanglin Wu, Yuyang Luo, Yueqing Liang, Kaiwen Shi, Yanfang Ye, Ali Payani, Kai Shu

entry.summary: Introduces LLMA-Mem, a lifelong memory framework for LLM multi-agent systems that jointly considers team size scaling and temporal learning ability, evaluated on MultiAgentBench across coding, research, and database tasks.

entry.title: CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge

author.name: Mete Ismayilzada, Renqing Cuomao, Daniil Yurshevich, Anna Sotnikova, Lonneke van der Plas, Antoine Bosselut

entry.summary: Introduces CresOWLve, a benchmark for evaluating creative problem-solving in LLMs using puzzles grounded in real-world knowledge, requiring logical reasoning, lateral thinking, analogy-making, and commonsense knowledge.

entry.title: Toward Executable Repository-Level Code Generation via Environment Alignment

author.name: Ruwei Pan, Junlei Shen, Linhao Wu, Yueheng Zhu, Zixiong Yang, Yakun Zhang, Lu Zhang, Hongyu Zhang

entry.summary: EnvGraph formulates repository-level code generation as an environment alignment problem, jointly modeling dependency resolution and execution environment compatibility for multi-file repository generation.

entry.title: CREBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Cryptographic Binary Reverse Engineering

author.name: Baicheng Chen, Yu Wang, Ziheng Zhou, Xiangru Liu, Juanru Li, Yilei Chen, Tianxing He

entry.summary: CREBench evaluates LLMs on cryptographic binary reverse engineering with 432 challenges from 48 crypto algorithms at 3 difficulty levels. Tests LLM capabilities for security-critical RE tasks.

entry.title: Can Humans Tell? A Dual-Axis Study of Human Perception of LLM-Generated News

author.name: Alexander Loth, Martin Kappes, Marc-Oliver Pahl

entry.summary: Study with 2,318 judgments from 1,054 participants shows humans cannot reliably distinguish LLM-generated from human-written news across six models. Domain expertise predicts accuracy but political orientation does not.

entry.title: Interpreting Video Representations with Spatio-Temporal Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Atahan Dokme, Sriram Vishwanath

entry.summary: First systematic study of Sparse Autoencoders on video representations, proposing spatio-temporal contrastive objectives and Matryoshka hierarchical grouping to maintain temporal coherence while achieving interpretability.

entry.title: VLA-Forget: Vision-Language-Action Unlearning for Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Ravi Ranjan, Agoritsa Polyzou

entry.summary: VLA-Forget addresses machine unlearning for vision-language-action robot models, recognizing that undesirable knowledge can be distributed across perception, alignment, and reasoning layers in embodied AI.

entry.title: From Paper to Program: A Multi-Stage LLM-Assisted Workflow for Accelerating Quantum Many-Body Algorithm Development

author.name: Yi Zhou

entry.summary: Multi-stage LLM workflow for translating quantum many-body theory into code, using LaTeX specifications as intermediate blueprints. Validated by generating a DMRG engine that accurately captures critical physics.

entry.title: Learning Robust Visual Features in Computed Tomography Enables Efficient Transfer Learning for Clinical Tasks

author.name: Rub\'en Moreno-Aguado, Alba Magall\'on, Victor Moreno, Yingying Fang, Guang Yang
